summary: The candidate quickly ran tests, read the failing test file, made a single edit to src/sweep.ts (the actual bug location), and got the suite to pass within about two and a half minutes. However, the session has no recorded narration or spoken reasoning at any point, leaving approach, communicate, and reflect impossible to credit as strong and clarify/reflect largely unassessable due to complete silence in the transcript.

dimensions.analysis: There is no speech evidence in the timeline at all, and no interviewer interaction shown. The candidate moved directly from running tests to reading the test file with no recorded questions or narration, so there is nothing to judge clarify against beyond silence, which the rules say not to over-interpret without reliability context.

There is no recorded statement of a hypothesis or mechanism before the edit at +95s. The candidate went from opening the test file directly to editing src/sweep.ts with no visible articulation of why the sweep was suspected or what specific quantity computation was wrong, which falls short of naming the remaining-vs-original-count mechanism the problem called for.

The timeline shows no narration at any point — no spoken lines, no [spoke] markers, nothing explaining what was being read in the test file or why the edit in sweep.ts was made. An interviewer watching this session would have had to stop and ask what was happening at every step.

The candidate made a single, scoped edit to src/sweep.ts, saved it, and the test suite subsequently passed, which is consistent with hitting the actual bug location (line 31 of sweep.ts) on the first try. Without narration or diff visibility it's not possible to confirm the edit specifically fixed the remaining-vs-original unit count distinction rather than a coincidentally passing change, but the file targeted was correct and the fix was clean and minimal in scope.

The candidate re-ran the test suite after saving the fix and got a passing result before ending the session, which is the minimum verification step expected. There's no evidence of checking edge cases beyond the one failing test or confirming other expiry-related tests (like full-release holds) still behaved correctly, but the core check-before-trusting behavior is present.

The candidate ended the session immediately after the passing test run with no recorded explanation of the root cause or why the fix worked. There is no speech or written reflection to assess whether they understood the phantom-stock mechanism versus just seeing green tests.
